scope: Validation, corpus analysis and literal question/answer extraction over the expanded non-Bashar candidate set of self-run baseline ASR transcripts produced from public YouTube audio stored under ${CHANNELS_ET_RAW_ROOT}/youtube-audio/<video_id>/ (acquisition.json + audio.mp3 + asr-receipt.json + ASR outputs). The build is gated on every record in research/acquisition-2026-11/all-candidates.json having a terminal state: completed hash-bound ASR, excluded_under_300, excluded_language_mismatch, or held_route_limit_over_150_minutes. Included + excluded + held must equal the complete candidate set; the original 13-video pilot is retained only as historical provenance.

sourceBoundaries.whatSourcesAre: Self-run baseline ASR of public YouTube audio. Audio was acquired through the ordinary public y2mate.gs paste-link interface (audio.mp3, sha256-receipted) and transcribed locally with the pinned Systran/faster-whisper-tiny.en model (revision 0d3d19a32d3338f10357c0889762bd8d64bbdeba, CPU int8, beam_size=1, VAD filter, condition_on_previous_text=false) in contiguous 300 s decode windows covering 100% of each file, timestamps offset-stitched. sourceType is public_youtube_audio_self_run_ASR; provider label is self_run_faster_whisper_tiny.en.
whatSourcesAreNot: Not rendered subtitles and not original caption tracks: this layer is independent ASR output from audio bytes, distinct from research/expansion-2026/non-bashar-analysis (provider-rendered subtitle text).
Not human validated: humanValidated == false; no human WER, no human peer review; tiny.en int8 CPU baseline accuracy is unmeasured.
Not diarized speaker turns: interviewer vs practitioner vs claimed-entity voice cannot be separated.
Not edition-equivalent to any YouTube caption track: no claim that ASR text matches any caption edition.
Not multilingual: the pinned model is English-only (tiny.en); non-English audio is unsupported and excluded with explicit evidence, never silently analyzed as English.
Window-boundary words can be split by the 300 s chunking; this is a recorded limitation of the transcription receipt.

nonClaims: No truth, reality or physical-origin assessment of any claimed entity; claimed-entity labels are publisher metadata only.
No cross-ET agreement, consensus or disagreement assessment; the Q&A layer records question TYPES and answer ORIENTATION only.

NMF/KMeans on 34 short ASR documents (43 terminal candidates including exclusions and a hold) are diagnostics only; no natural clusters, no stable semantic structure and no population significance are claimed. All base and stability runs converged before the 1,200-iteration cap in the final expanded build; iteration counts remain exported.
Manual review is AI review (manualReviewKind=ai_agent_review), not human annotation; humanValidated stays false.
Uploader, practitioner and claimed entity are kept as three distinct metadata roles; none is equated with another.

Detected language is a text heuristic over the ASR output; the degenerate-output guard (words-per-minute and repetition evidence) exists because an English-only model forced onto unsupported audio emits repetitive hallucinated English rather than a faithful transcript.

inputs.priorRenderedEditionIndex: research/expansion-2026/non-bashar-analysis/sources-index.csv (language cross-edition notes only; never used as transcript text)

checks: directory name == candidate video_id == acquisition.video_id == receipt.videoId; sourceUrl contains the video id and matches the candidate list
acquisition.json status == completed; audio.mp3 exists, is not a symlink, and its sha256/bytes match acquisition.json

asr-receipt.json status == completed; sourceType == public_youtube_audio_self_run_ASR; audioSha256 == audio file hash; settings equal the pinned expected settings (language en, beam_size 1, vad_filter true, condition_on_previous_text false, device cpu, compute_type int8, modelId Systran/faster-whisper-tiny.en, manifest revision, chunkSeconds 300) and settingsSha256 recomputes
every outputSha256 entry in the receipt recomputes against the on-disk asr-transcript.txt / asr-segments.jsonl / asr-transcript.srt

segment records use start/end/text (normalized to startSeconds/endSeconds for analysis); every record has numeric 0 <= start < end, non-empty text, non-decreasing starts; receipt segmentCount == jsonl line count; receipt wordCount == whitespace words of asr-transcript.txt; SRT cue count == segmentCount

durations: |acquisition.duration_seconds - receipt.ffprobeDurationSeconds| <= 0.5 s; |receipt.decodedDurationSeconds - ffprobeDurationSeconds| <= 1.0 s; chunksProcessed * 300 >= decodedDurationSeconds (full-length decode); ASR text coverage = lastSegmentEnd / ffprobeDurationSeconds must be >= 0.75 (VAD speech-free tails are legitimate); coverage in [0.75, 0.95) or > 1.0 is a non-fatal note
ledger record exists with status completed and matching sha256/bytes/duration_seconds (<= 0.5 s)

asr-summary.json shows each completed acquisition completed with audioSha256 and outputSha256 matching the on-disk receipt; explicit under-300/language exclusions and the route-limit hold are validated separately (gate for the whole candidate set)
title/publisher/practitionerContext/claimedGroup match the candidate list (uploader != practitioner != claimed entity kept as distinct roles)

language: script-aware detection over ASR text must yield English (pinned model is English-only); degenerate-output guard excludes sources whose ASR output is not a usable English transcript (words-per-minute below 45 over the audio duration, the observed signature of tiny.en forced onto non-English audio is repetitive hallucinated English at ~21 wpm versus 110-156 wpm for English audio)
inclusionValidation.exclusionRule: Any failed fatal check excludes the record from included analysis and records the reason; missing/mismatched audio, transcript, duration or unsupported language are fatal. The build gate refuses final outputs until all candidates resolve to completed ASR, explicit exclusion, or the route-limit hold. Holds are never counted as analyzed.

segmentIndex.granularity: one row per ASR segment with exact start/end seconds and exact text; private only
segmentIndex.publicExposure: metadata, counts and sha256 hashes only; no transcript bodies in the repository

corpusAnalysis.tokenization: lowercase Unicode letter tokens (>=2 chars); per-document stoplist selected by detectedLanguage (English for all included sources; German/compact-Arabic paths retained for defense in depth); proper names excluded from TF-IDF/NMF; per-document raw/analysis token counts exported in tokenizationDiagnostics; sources-index word_count is whitespace-delimited
corpusAnalysis.tfidf: unigram+bigram TF-IDF (sublinear_tf), deterministic top terms per corpus and per publisher/practitioner/claimed-entity overlay
corpusAnalysis.nmf: NMF k=6 (n_components bounded by corpus size), init=nndsvda, seed 20261110, max_iter=1200; seed stability over 10 random-init seeds reported as mean best-match cosine of topic-term vectors. Iteration counts and convergence are exported; all runs converged before the cap in the final expanded build
corpusAnalysis.kmeans: KMeans k swept 2..8, silhouette diagnostics over 10 seeds, and adjusted Rand index vs the base seed over the other nine seeds only; the trivial base-vs-itself ARI=1 comparison is excluded and ariComparisons=9 for every k

documentNetwork.weakestEdgeRule: each node with a positive-similarity neighbor keeps its strongest edge even below threshold; all-zero nodes remain isolated. This is a visualization rule, not evidence of substantive similarity

corpusAnalysis.temporalDurationProfiles: per-source duration, segment and word rates (words/segments per minute), question-unit rates per 10 minutes; ASR segment cadence differs from rendered-subtitle cue cadence and is reported as-is
corpusAnalysis.sensitivity: proper-name and commercial-pattern counts per document; commercial regex is English-oriented, not a cross-language advertisement detector

questionExtraction.sentenceSplit: regex split after [.!?] followed by whitespace (Arabic marks retained for defense in depth though tiny.en never emits them)
questionExtraction.questionBearingSegment: ASR segment containing at least one sentence with ASCII '?'

mergeRule.description: Adjacent question-bearing segments separated by <= 2.0 s are merged into one question unit; all question sentences inside the unit are preserved with their count.

questionFormCodebook.tag_question: whole question sentence is a discourse tag (right?, you know?, does that make sense?, ...)
questionFormCodebook.imperative_prompt: imperative elicitation (tell me/us about, talk about, explain, describe, walk us through, can you tell/share/explain ...)
questionFormCodebook.yes_no_question: auxiliary + subject inversion pattern (do you, are they, is it, can we, ...)
questionFormCodebook.other_unclassified_qmark: carries '?' but matches none of the above transparent English patterns; conservative default
questionFormCodebook.tag_only: unit whose question sentences are all tags (unit-level primary form)

questionExtraction.primaryFormRule: unit primary form = form of the first non-tag question sentence, else tag_only

discourseClassCodebook.unclear_dialogue_context: DEFAULT; no explicit textual evidence about who is being asked (no diarization).
discourseClassCodebook.direct_interview_candidate: PROMOTED only on explicit textual evidence: imperative elicitation pattern or second-person / session-subject address (you/your or entity/channeling reference) in a wh/yes-no/other unit. AI review may promote additional candidates with bounded notes.
discourseClassCodebook.rhetorical_candidate: all question sentences are discourse tags, or the question is immediately answered by the same segment flow without an addressee cue.
discourseClassCodebook.secondary_report: question text reports someone else's asking (people ask, he/she asked, I get asked, ...).
discourseClassCodebook.self_report: speaker reports asking themselves (I ask myself, I wonder, ...).

questionExtraction.caution: Without diarization these classes are textual heuristics only; AI review refines all candidates when <= 60, else a stratified >= 60 sample. Speaker turns are never invented.

answerWindow.rule: after the question unit end, take following non-question segments until the first of: 4 segments collected, 90 s elapsed since question end, or the next question-bearing segment (stop before it)

statusCodebook.complete_line_cap: 4 non-question segments collected; 'complete' means the extraction window filled, not that the speaker finished the answer
statusCodebook.interrupted_by_next_question: a following question begins; window may hold 0+ answer segments
statusCodebook.end_of_transcript_boundary_unknown: transcript ended before the window filled; true answer boundary unknown
statusCodebook.no_answer_window: next segment is already a question; no answer text captured
statusCodebook.no_answer_end_of_transcript: question ends the transcript; unanswered / boundary unknown

orientationCodebook.process_practice_oriented: answer window dominated by practice/process/inner-work verbs (focus, breathe, allow, practice, meditate, align, release, integrate)
orientationCodebook.descriptive_explanatory: answer has a positive descriptive/explanatory pattern match; zero-pattern answers are not placed here by default
orientationCodebook.unclassified_default: answer window exists but matches none of the four orientation patterns; this is an explicit unclassified bucket, not positive descriptive evidence
orientationCodebook.conditional_hedged: answer dominated by conditionals/hedges (depends, may, might, could, if you, in your timing, not yet)
orientationCodebook.timing_specific: answer gives explicit timing/window language (dates, years, soon, in the coming, within)
orientationCodebook.not_assessed_language: answer text exists but the English orientation codebook is not applied to an unsupported language

answerWindow.orientationCaution: Orientation describes the shape of the captured answer text only. It says nothing about answer truth, agreement across entities, or consensus, which are never assessed.

questionFamilyCodebook.contact_timing: when/how open contact, disclosure timing, first contact
questionFamilyCodebook.dna_origins: DNA, genetics, origins, ancestry, hybrid, lineage, starseed origins
questionFamilyCodebook.ascension: ascension, 5D/fifth density, shift, new earth, frequency raising, dimensions
questionFamilyCodebook.reality_agency: nature of reality, manifestation, belief, free will, agency, creating reality
questionFamilyCodebook.healing: healing, health, disease, body symptoms, energy healing
questionFamilyCodebook.dreams_contact: dreams, astral, sleep contact, visitation in dreams
questionFamilyCodebook.predictions: future events, prophecies, dates, solar flash, eclipse, event predictions
questionFamilyCodebook.other_theme: none of the above dominant families
questionFamilyCodebook.not_assessed_language: question is preserved literally, but the English family codebook is not applied to an unsupported language

commonQuestionFamilies.familyKey: sha256-16 of sorted unique lowercase content tokens of the question sentences (stoplist and proper-name list removed); null when no content tokens remain. Interrogative stopwords are applied uniformly (what/who/whom/whose/which as well as when/where/why/how), preventing a one-token wh-word family. Tag-only and all other stopword-only units stay family-less in the public rows and are excluded from family grouping, so no spurious empty-key common question is created
commonQuestionFamilies.repostRisk: review flag only: high if the same family key appears in >= 2 distinct publishers, medium if >= 2 videos of one publisher, else low. Token-key recurrence is not semantic equivalence or a repost finding. recurrence_scope distinguishes cross_video, within_single_video and singleton rows.

manualReview.sampleSize: all extracted candidates when <= 60, else a stratified >= 60 sample across available claimed-entity labels
checks: rhetorical vs direct vs secondary classification
manualReview.storage: manual-review.json (bounded paraphrase notes + excerpts <= 150 chars + sha256 only; full text stays private)

limitsAttachedToEveryFigure: Self-run baseline ASR (faster-whisper tiny.en int8 CPU, English-only, 300 s windows) over public YouTube audio; not rendered subtitles or original caption tracks; no diarization; no human WER; humanValidated=false; ASR accuracy unmeasured; modest corpus (34 included documents; 43 terminal candidates); uploader != practitioner != claimed entity; claimed-entity labels are publisher metadata only.
